issues.description: The template's StockIngredient class defines a constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean) while the problem statement UML and the solution expect StockIngredient(String, int, int). This mismatch will prevent students from creating new StockIngredient instances as described in the task (e.g., new StockIngredient(name, price, quantity)) and will block implementing acceptSupplyDelivery according to the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a 3-parameter constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) in the template (either by adding an overloaded constructor that delegates to the existing one or by changing the existing constructor signature) so it matches the UML/problem description and the solution. This will allow students to instantiate StockIngredient as specified and implement acceptSupplyDelivery without signature conflicts.
